_comment: Declared derivation for this record: text.txt == extract -> slice -> reflow -> mechanical -> corrections, byte-exact against text_sha256. Verified by scripts/derive_text.py. Every human repair of an extraction defect is recorded here with a reason, so nothing about the derivation lives only in the stored bytes.

extractor._reason: The stored original is the govinfo plain-text rendering of 51 U.S.C. ch. 513, so no PDF extraction is involved.

slice._reason: govinfo prefixes the text with its own provenance banner ('Source: U.S. Government Publishing Office, United States Code, 2015 Edition, ...') followed by a blank line. That banner is govinfo's description OF the document, not part of the enacted text, so it is cut. Recorded here because the extraction recipe previously said slice:null, which was factually wrong.

_verified.note: No human repairs were needed for this record — the only difference between the stored original and text.txt is the sliced govinfo banner. It is the simplest record in the corpus and was used to prove the pipeline.
